story: I resigned from Brightwave Pvt Ltd in Pune, Maharashtra on 30 September 2026. They have not paid my September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000. I have my offer letter and salary slips.

timeline.user_words: I resigned from Brightwave Pvt Ltd in Pune, Maharashtra on 30 September 2026.
They have not paid my September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000.

facts.user_goal: To receive the unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000.

rules.name: wage_due_date
rules.message: After your last day (30 Sep 2026), the law says final wages must be paid within two working days - about 03 Oct 2026 (not counting Sundays and national holidays; your State can set a different limit).
rules.label: When final pay was due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 03 Oct 2029 (1060 days left). This counts 3 years from 03 Oct 2026 (when September 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 42,000 = Rs 42,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your employer Brightwave Pvt Ltd must pay your final September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000 within two working days of your resignation on 30 September 2026, which is about 3 October 2026. Since they have not paid, you can file a wage claim before your State labour department. The claim must be filed within three years from 3 October 2026. The employer must prove they paid you.

claims.text: The employer must pay your final wages within two working days of your resignation.
Your unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000 counts as wages.
You can file a wage claim before the wage authority within three years from when the wages became due.
The employer must prove they paid you.

support.text: The employer must pay your final wages within two working days of your resignation.
support.reason: Section 17(2) explicitly states that where an employee has resigned, 'the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his... resignation.'

support.text: Your unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000 counts as wages.
support.reason: Section 2(y) defines 'wages' as 'all remuneration whether by way of salaries, allowances or otherwise, expressed in terms of money or capable of being so expressed' and includes 'basic pay' and 'dearness allowance'. The unpaid September 2026 salary of Rs 42,000 falls within this definition of wages.

support.text: You can file a wage claim before the wage authority within three years from when the wages became due.
support.reason: Section 45(6) explicitly states that 'The application under sub-section (4) may be filed within a period of three years from the date on which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises.'

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you.
support.reason: Section 59 explicitly states that 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer' in cases of non-payment of wages or less payment of wages.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: Brightwave Pvt Ltd, [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for payment of unpaid wages

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 42,000. My wages for September 2026 have not been paid. My last working day was 30 September 2026.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 42,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: Offer letter, Salary slips.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
